newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile Chispa stocks climb on Endesa deal.
newsitem.headline: Chile Chispa stocks climb on Endesa deal.

text.p: The Chispa group of companies climbed sharply in early trade on news of the $1.5 billion deal between Spanish utility Endesa and power investment company Enersis, said dealers.
The five Chispa firms own a 29 percent stake in Enersis, which in turn controls Chile's largest generator Endesa.
"It's a huge vote of confidence in Enersis. It looks like the Spaniards are paying a significant premium for the shares," said one analyst.
Luz y Fuerza rallied 9.19 percent in the first hour of trading to 190 pesos. Luz A was up 7.89 percent at 410 pesos with Chispados rising 6.15 percent to 190 pesos.
Under the deal the Spanish utility will offer to buy the Chispa group A-series of shares, and then buy the B-series stock in two separate tranches.
The Chispa shares have rallied in recent weeks on speculation of the deal, the largest investment by a foreign company in Chile's booming energy industry.
Enersis opened slightly higher, with investors waiting for more details of the pact to see how it will affect the holding company, said traders.
"The big question now is what will happen to Enersis management," said one trader.
